What is Bacterial Canker and how do I treat it?

Hello there! Bacterial Canker is a serious disease in tomatoes caused by the bacteria *Clavibacter michiganensis* subsp. *michiganensis*. Honestly, this is one of the trickier ones to diagnose early because the initial wilting can just look like a thirsty plant. It's quite stubborn too—it can survive up to five years in plant debris! Ah, wonderful! Ji, that "unilateral wilting" is such a characteristic symptom. It happens because the bacteria multiplies and blocks the vascular tissue—the plant's plumbing system—on just one side of the leaflet. Since there isn't a chemical "cure" once the plant is infected, management is all about prevention. For instance, commercial growers focus heavily on planting clean transplants and sowing only certified bacteria-free seed.
